name: read_note
description: Read and return the content of a note by its relative path in the vault. To read only one section of a note, pass heading.

heading.description: Only this section: the heading's text without the #s, e.g. 'Notes'; note_outline lists a note's headings.

name: read_notes
description: Read several notes at once. Returns each note's content under a '## <path>' heading.

name: create_note
description: Create a new note at the given path with the provided content. A name cannot contain : < > " | ? * (write 11.00 or 1100 for a time).

name: update_note
description:
Replace a note's entire content (destructive): anything not included in content is lost. Use edit_note to
change a part of the note, or append_to_note to add to its end.

name: edit_note
description: Replace an exact piece of text inside a note, leaving the rest untouched. old_text must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true; line endings and spaces at the ends of lines do not count.

name: append_to_note
description: Append text to the end of an existing note.

heading.description: Append at the end of this section instead

name: delete_note
description:
Delete a note or attachment (destructive). By default it moves to the vault's .trash folder and can be restored;
permanent=true removes it for good.

name: list_notes
description: List the notes in a folder, with its subfolders first (ending in '/'); with recursive, every note below it. A folder may be named by its last part when that is unique. A long list is cut off after *limit* entries and says how many it left out.

sort.description: name, or modified: newest first, with dates

name: find_notes
description: Find notes by file name or path. Supports * wildcards ('*2026-09*', 'Projects/*', which finds that folder at any depth); without a wildcard the pattern matches anywhere in the path, case-insensitively.

sort.description: name, or modified: newest first, with dates

name: list_attachments
description: List the vault's attachments: the files that are not notes, such as images, PDFs, recordings, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, canvases and CSV files, each with its type and size. path narrows the list to a folder and its subfolders; pattern filters by name with * wildcards, as in find_notes ('*invoice*', '*.pdf'). Read one with read_attachment.

sort.description: name, or modified: newest first, with dates

name: move_note
description:
Move or rename a note or attachment within the vault (destructive). By default every [[wikilink]] pointing at it
is updated, so links do not break.

name: search_vault
description:
Search notes for a case-insensitive substring. Optionally restrict to notes carrying *tag*
(frontmatter or inline #tag) or living under *folder*; with only a tag or folder, every match is listed.

name: list_tags
description: List the tags used in the vault with the number of notes carrying each.

name: get_backlinks
description: Find all notes that link to the given note using [[wikilink]] syntax.

name: get_outlinks
description: Extract all [[wikilink]] outgoing links from a note.

name: list_tasks
description:
List checkbox tasks (`- [ ] …`) written inside notes. status is todo, done or all; path narrows it to
one note or folder. Returns 'note:line: - [ ] text' lines. TaskNotes task notes are separate files —
use list_tasknotes for those.

name: daily_note
description:
The path of the daily note for a date (today when empty), as Obsidian is configured to name and file
it. Read it with read_note; it does not have to exist yet.

name: note_outline
description:
The headings of a note as an indented tree — a cheap way to see how a long note is built before
reading or editing it.

name: find_broken_links
description:
Links pointing at notes that do not exist, as 'note -> missing target' lines. Use it to clean up a
vault after moving or deleting notes.

name: create_from_template
description:
Create a note from one of the vault's templates, with the template's variables (date, title, …)
filled in by Obsidian. Use list_templates to see what exists.

name: list_templates
description: The templates configured in this vault, one name per line.

name: open_in_obsidian
description: Show a note to the user in Obsidian — use it after changing something they will want to look at.

name: query_base
description:
Run an Obsidian Base and return its rows, as its filters, formulas and sorting give them. Pass base (a .base file) or definition (a Base's YAML, such as the content of a ```base block, with note set to the note it is in). view picks one of the Base's views; limit caps the rows.
Examples: {"base": "Tasks - Open by project", "view": "Open tasks"}, or for the tasks that link to a note: {"definition": "filters: 'file.hasTag(\"task\") && file.hasLink(this.file)'", "note": "Projects/Plan.md"}

view.description: The view to run, by its name, e.g. 'Board'; without it, the Base's first view.

limit.description: Rows to return, 50 by default. For more, e.g. all rows of a large Base, set it higher, e.g. 100; the answer says how many rows there are.

note.description: For a definition from a note: that note, which 'this' in it refers to

name: list_tasknotes
description:
List TaskNotes tasks — notes with task frontmatter, one file per task — with status, dates and
project. status is open (the default), done or all; project narrows it to one project, and
project="none" lists the tasks that belong to no project at all. The answer says how many tasks the
filters left out and caps a long list, so it is never mistaken for everything there is. Checkbox tasks
written inside notes are a different thing: use list_tasks.

name: create_tasknote
description:
Create a TaskNotes task. scheduled is the day the work is planned for ("scheduled for", "on",
"tomorrow"); due is the deadline ("due", "by", "deadline") — set only what was asked for. Dates are
YYYY-MM-DD (or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM); projects, contexts and tags are comma separated; estimate is in minutes;
recurrence is an RRULE. The plugin files the note where this vault keeps tasks and fills in the defaults,
so do not write task notes by hand.

name: complete_tasknote
description:
Mark a TaskNotes task as done: sets the vault's completed status and today's completion date. A task
that recurs is not completed here — advancing its schedule is the plugin's job.

name: get_metadata
description: Load and return YAML frontmatter metadata from a note as JSON.

name: update_metadata
description:
Set, update or remove a single frontmatter property of a note. The value **replaces** the old one, so to add
to a list pass the whole list — read the note first and write '["task", "office"]', not '["office"]',
or the tag that was there is gone. Types are read from the value: 'true' and 'false' become checkboxes,
numbers become numbers, a list becomes a list whether it is written as JSON or the way frontmatter writes
it ('[task, office]'), and anything else, including a bare [[wikilink]], is text. Quote a value ("true")
to store it as text. The result says what was stored. An unquoted null removes the property.

name: read_attachment
description:
Read an attachment file from the vault. PDF files are returned as their text when they have a text layer, and otherwise rendered page-by-page as images; as_text chooses. Image
files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, bmp, tiff) are returned as images, video files (mp4, webm, avi,
mov, mkv) are sampled as frames via ffmpeg plus a transcript of their audio track, and audio
recordings (m4a, mp3, wav, ogg, opus, flac, aac, audio-only webm) are transcribed to timestamped
text. Transcripts are saved below the recording's embed and reused on later calls. You may pass a bare filename (e.g. 'photo.jpg') and
the tool will locate the file anywhere in the vault automatically. Office documents (docx, xlsx, pptx), OpenDocument (odt, ods, odp), EPUB books, canvases and text files (csv, json, txt, …) are returned as text; pages picks the sheets, slides or chapters.

pages.description: PDF pages, sheets, slides or chapters, e.g. '2' or '1-3'

as_text.description: A PDF's text (true) or its pages as images (false). Left out, the text when the PDF has a text layer, which is far smaller and the way to read or search its words; images are for scans, charts and layout.

name: update_user_memory
description: Update a section of the persistent user profile with new information you've learned about the user. Use this when you discover facts worth remembering across sessions: preferences, identity, projects, communication style, or specific facts.

section.description: The profile section to update. One of: 'Identity', 'Preferences', 'Projects & Context', 'Communication Style', 'Learned Facts'.

content.description: The new content for this section. Will replace the existing section content.

name: read_user_memory
description: Read the full persistent user profile — what you know about the user so far.

name: web_fetch
description: Fetch the text content of a URL. Returns the page content as plain text or markdown.
